questions.stem: A shopkeeper buys a toy for Rs. 500 and sells it to a customer for Rs. 600. What is his precise profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 500. Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 600. Profit = SP - CP = 600 - 500 = Rs. 100. Profit Percentage = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (100 / 500) × 100 = 20%.

questions.stem: An article is sold at a loss of 10% for exactly Rs. 900. What is the original cost price of the article?
questions.explanation: Let the Cost Price be CP. Selling at a 10% loss means the Selling Price is 90% of CP. So, 0.90 × CP = 900. CP = 900 / 0.90 = Rs. 1000.

questions.stem: By selling a vintage clock for Rs. 240, a man incurs a loss of 10%. At what exact price should he sell it so that he makes a clear profit of 20%?
questions.explanation: SP = 240. Loss = 10%. This means 90% of CP = 240, so CP = 240 / 0.9 = 800/3. To make a 20% profit, the new SP must be 120% of CP. New SP = 1.2 × (800/3) = (12/10) × (800/3) = 4 × 80 = Rs. 320.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper allows a flat discount of 10% on the marked price of an item but still manages to gain 8%. If the marked price is Rs. 360, what is the exact cost price?
questions.explanation: Marked Price (MP) = 360. Discount = 10%. Selling Price (SP) = MP - 10% of MP = 360 - 36 = 324. The shopkeeper gains 8%, so SP = 108% of CP. 1.08 × CP = 324. CP = 324 / 1.08 = 300. Thus, Cost Price is Rs. 300.

questions.stem: A dishonest dealer publicly professes to sell his goods exactly at cost price, but he secretly uses a false weight of 900 grams for a 1 kg weight. Find his true gain percentage.
questions.explanation: The dealer claims to sell 1000g at its cost price, but he actually delivers only 900g. His cost is for 900g, but he gets paid for 1000g. His profit is 100g on an investment of 900g. Gain % = (Profit / Cost) × 100 = (100 / 900) × 100 = 100/9 % = 11 and 1/9 %.

questions.stem: A man sells two antique chairs for exactly Rs. 1200 each. On one transaction, he gains exactly 20%, and on the other, he loses exactly 20%. What is his overall net gain or loss percentage on the entire transaction?
questions.explanation: When two items are sold at the identical selling price and there is a gain of x% on one and a loss of x% on the other, there is always a net loss. The net loss percentage is given by the formula: (x / 10)² %. Here, x = 20. Loss % = (20 / 10)² = 2² = 4%. Thus, there is a 4% overall loss.

questions.stem: The cost price of 12 articles is exactly equal to the selling price of 9 articles. Simultaneously, the discount offered on 10 articles is exactly equal to the profit earned on 5 articles. Find the absolute difference between the profit percentage and the discount percentage.
questions.explanation: 1) 12 CP = 9 SP => SP/CP = 12/9 = 4/3. Let CP = 3 units, SP = 4 units. Profit (P) = SP - CP = 1 unit. Profit % = (1/3) × 100 = 33.33%. 2) 10 Discount (D) = 5 Profit (P) => D = P/2. Since P = 1 unit, D = 0.5 units. Marked Price (MP) = SP + D = 4 + 0.5 = 4.5 units. Discount % = (D/MP) × 100 = (0.5/4.5) × 100 = 1/9 × 100 = 11.11%. Difference = 33.33% - 11.11% = 22.22%.
